# RC Surface

> RC Surface is an extension for Ableton Live that serves a control surface in the browser of a phone. The computer runs the server on the local network over HTTPS/WSS, and the phone scans a QR code and opens the page. Nothing is installed on the phone, and nothing goes through the cloud.

## Overview

- **Controls.** 12 performance pads with modes A/B/C/D (momentary, hold, toggle, burst), two independent Static/Physics XY panels, 8 knobs, 8 faders, 8 toggles **T1–T8** with **Square** pulses and 8 snapshots with timed and vector (XY) morph.
- **Sensors.** Motion and orientation, the phone microphone or a selected audio input (RMS, envelope, gate, attack and twelve audio descriptors such as transient, kick, snare, brightness and K-weighted low/mid/high loudness), and single-hand camera tracking with MediaPipe Hands (bundled, works offline).
- **Mapping.** From the phone (**MAP**) or the panel inside Live, any control can be bound to a Live parameter (tracks, returns, main, devices), to a fixed MIDI trigger note on a MIDI track through the bundled Max for Live receiver `RC-Midi-Receiver.amxd`, or to **Launch Clip** (launch Session clip, advance clip list, or stop track via AbletonOSC, with optional **After it starts** rules). Curves, ranges, soft takeover and signal-loss behaviour are set per mapping.
- **Pages.** The phone has seven pages: **PERF**, **MIX**, **SNP**, **SNS**, **AUD**, **VID** and **REC**. **MAP** is an overlay. **AUT** is the **PERF** header mode for XY loops: **SYNC** 1–5 bars or **FREE** 1–30 seconds in steps of one second.
- **Recording.** **REC** verifies the armed input set through **ARM / SOLO / MUTE** cards (with live volume knobs and inline double-click rename), a bar/beat marker timeline with **ZOOM**, **START**/**END** (`1–10` passes or `∞`, or **FREE** until **STOP**) and pre-roll OFF/1/2/4. **Punch In** is temporary, and owned cleanup never replays after loss.
- **Recording to a clip.** **REC** also selects **CLIP**: an explicitly empty Session scene for all armed inputs, native 1/2/4/8/16-bar length, Global/None/1bar/1beat quantization, and **BACK TO ARR** when idle. **CLIP STOP** preserves **ARM** and the global transport, and stops only still-owned targets, with observed pending/unknown states and no reconnect replay. There is no existing-clip overdub and no take/comp browser.
- **Configuration.** **CFG** opens only by tapping **CFG** at the top of the phone; holding a pad or another control does not open it.
- **Automation.** **AUT** warnings appear once, in the yellow toast.
- **Vision.** **VID** supports fifteen learned-pose cards with 3-6 examples each and advisory **RETAKE**/**KEEP**. **PALM** and **FACE** are normalized **MAP** inputs. **FACE** reads the palm and back orientation of the hand, not facial tracking. Missing or invalid values follow **Safe loss**.
- **Panel.** The **Main** tab of the Live panel shows the QR code and the connected clients. The addresses and the certificate are in the **Network** tab.
- **Certificates.** A local certificate authority of this computer signs the server certificate for localhost and for the private addresses of the network. The **Certificate** section of the **Network** tab links an install page on the HTTPS port + 1, so the phone and the computer install it once and the browser stops warning. An address pinned with **USE** keeps a self-signed certificate.
- **Storage.** Projects, presets and mappings live in `storageDirectory/surface-v2/` with schema 2, and data from 1.x is neither imported nor deleted.
- **Architecture.** The host side runs on the Ableton Extensions SDK in TypeScript, and the phone side in plain browser JavaScript. The transport is HTTPS/WSS with rotating session tokens, meant for a trusted studio or home network.

## Requirements

- Ableton Live 12.4.5+ Suite (Beta) with the official Extensions SDK.
- A phone on the same local network: iOS 15.4+ Safari or Chromium on Android, held in landscape.
- **AbletonOSC** (UDP `11000`/`11001`) is optional; **REC**, **Launch Clip**, **TRN**, **AUT** in **SYNC** and **Deep Sync** need it.
- Reported use is not an exhaustive hardware or latency certification.

## Unsupported versions and platforms

- Ableton Live 11 or earlier.
- Other DAWs.
- More than one controlling phone at a time.
- Linux hosts.

## Licence

PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, free for noncommercial use and not open source in the OSI sense. RC Surface is an independent project by Gabriel Worm, not affiliated with Ableton AG.

## Documentation

- [Landing page](https://ntworm.github.io/rc-surface/): the surface map, the control inventory, the install steps and the troubleshooting.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntworm/rc-surface/main/README.md): the features, the quick start, the architecture and the development commands.
- [Install guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntworm/rc-surface/main/docs/INSTALL.md): installing the `.ablx`, connecting the phone, the certificates, AbletonOSC, the Max devices and the troubleshooting.
- [User guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntworm/rc-surface/main/docs/USER-GUIDE.md): every page of the phone controller, the pad modes, **T1–T8**/**Square**, **MAP**, **AUT**, **CFG**, **REC**, the snapshots, the sensors, the audio descriptors and the vision.
- [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntworm/rc-surface/main/docs/FAQ.md): compatibility, latency, privacy, pricing and the common questions.
- [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntworm/rc-surface/main/docs/SECURITY.md): the threat model, the tokens, the certificates and the network exposure.
- [Privacy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntworm/rc-surface/main/docs/PRIVACY.md): what data exists and where it stays.
